```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidypopgen)
```

```{r set-directories, include=FALSE}
res_dir <- "../results/s04_full_pca/"
```

# Load gt

```{r}
mad_bor_g1000_sum <-
  gt_load("../data/intermediate/rbind_data/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_clean_ld.gt")
```

# Loci and sample count

```{r}
nrow(mad_bor_g1000_sum)
count_loci(mad_bor_g1000_sum)
```

# Count individuals from each group 

```{r}
malagasy_data <- subset(
  mad_bor_g1000_sum,
  mad_bor_g1000_sum$population %in% c(
    "Mikea", "Vezo",
    "Temoro", "Diego",
    "Merina",
    "Betsimisaraka",
    "Sakalava_Tsimihety",
    "Betsileo"
  )
)
nrow(malagasy_data)
```

# Impute

```{r}
gt_set_imputed(mad_bor_g1000_sum, TRUE)
```


# Compute PCA

```{r}
random_pca <- gt_pca_autoSVD(mad_bor_g1000_sum)
pcs <- as.data.frame(random_pca$u)
variance <- tidy(random_pca)
```

# Add population metadata

```{r}
pop_names <-
  read.csv("../data/raw/data_input/igsr-1000-genomes-phase-3-release.tsv",
    sep = "\t"
  )

# find matching id in pop_names Sample.name and mad_bor_g1000_sum id
# for the matches, replace the population with the population in pop_names
for (i in seq_len(nrow(pop_names))) {
  if (pop_names$Sample.name[i] %in% mad_bor_g1000_sum$id) {
    mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$id == pop_names$Sample.name[i], "population"] <- pop_names$Population.name[i]
  }
}

# replace "Luhya,Luhya" with "Luhya"
mad_bor_g1000_sum$population[mad_bor_g1000_sum$population == "Luhya,Luhya"] <- "Luhya"
# replace "Esan,Esan" with "Esan"
mad_bor_g1000_sum$population[mad_bor_g1000_sum$population == "Esan,Esan"] <- "Esan"
# replace "Gambian Mandinka,Gambian" with "Gambian Mandinka"
mad_bor_g1000_sum$population[mad_bor_g1000_sum$population == "Gambian Mandinka,Gambian"] <- "Gambian Mandinka"
# replace "Mende,Mende" with "Mende"
mad_bor_g1000_sum$population[mad_bor_g1000_sum$population == "Mende,Mende"] <- "Mende"
# replace "Kinh,Kinh Vietnamese" with "Kinh Vietnamese"
mad_bor_g1000_sum$population[mad_bor_g1000_sum$population == "Kinh,Kinh Vietnamese"] <- "Kinh Vietnamese"
# replcae "Punjabi,Punjabi" with "Punjabi"
mad_bor_g1000_sum$population[mad_bor_g1000_sum$population == "Punjabi,Punjabi"] <- "Punjabi"
# replcae "Benga,Bengali" with "Bengali"
mad_bor_g1000_sum$population[mad_bor_g1000_sum$population == "Bengali,Bengali"] <- "Bengali"

# replace any _ with a space
mad_bor_g1000_sum$population <- gsub("_", " ", mad_bor_g1000_sum$population)
```

# Plot PCA

```{r}
# create a new factor column with Malagasy populations as 1 and others as 0
mad_bor_g1000_sum$malagasy <- 0
all_malagasy <- subset(
  mad_bor_g1000_sum,
  population %in% c(
    "Betsimisaraka", "Merina", "Diego",
    "Sakalava Tsimihety", "Betsileo",
    "Vezo", "Mikea", "Temoro"
  )
)
mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$id %in% all_malagasy$id, "malagasy"] <- 1

# create Region
mad_bor_g1000_sum$Region <- "Other"
mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$population %in% c("Borneo", "Sumba", "Timor"), "Region"] <- "Island southeast Asia"
mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$population %in% c("Bengali", "Punjabi"), "Region"] <- "South Asia"
mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$population %in% c("Southern Han Chinese", "Kinh Vietnamese"), "Region"] <- "East Asia"
mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$population %in% c("Esan", "Gambian Mandinka", "Luhya", "Mende", "Yoruba"), "Region"] <- "Africa"
mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$malagasy == 1, "Region"] <- mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$malagasy == 1, "population"]
# wharerver is left as "Other" set to Africa
mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$Region == "Other", "Region"] <- "Africa"



ggplot(pcs, aes(x = V1, y = V2, colour = mad_bor_g1000_sum$Region)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = NULL,
    x = paste0("PC 1 (", round(variance$percent[1], 2), "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC 2 (", round(variance$percent[2], 2), "%)"),
    colour = "Population"
  ) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE, size = 2)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.text = element_text(size = 5),
    axis.line = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white")
  )
```

This PCA uses the KING relatedness filtering of 0.088, equivalent to second degree relatives, filtered within each population. 

Unbalanced sample sizes will cause bias in the dimensions of this first plot. To explore how this might be affecting the PCA, the next dataset will randomly subsample populations with more individuals down to equivalent sizes.

# Create a dataset with broadly equal sample sizes

```{r}
set.seed(1)

subsample <- function(x) {
  if (nrow(x) <= 30) {
    return(x$id)
  } else {
    x <- sample_n(x, size = 30)
    return(x$id)
  }
}

keep <- mad_bor_g1000_sum %>%
  group_by(population) %>%
  group_map(~ {
    if (!(.y$population %in% c(
      "Betsimisaraka", "Merina", "Diego",
      "Sakalava Tsimihety", "Betsileo",
      "Vezo", "Mikea", "Temoro"
    ))) {
      subsample(.x)
    } else {
      .x$id
    }
  })

mad_bor_g1000_sum <- mad_bor_g1000_sum %>% filter(id %in% unlist(keep))

if (file.exists("../data/intermediate/rbind_data/mad_bor_g1000_sum_clean_neo_ld_subsampled.gt")) {
  file.remove("../data/intermediate/rbind_data/mad_bor_g1000_sum_clean_neo_ld_subsampled.gt")
}
gt_save(
  mad_bor_g1000_sum,
  "../data/intermediate/rbind_data/mad_bor_g1000_sum_clean_neo_ld_subsampled.gt"
)
```

# Plot PCA

```{r}
# create a new factor column with Malagasy populations as 1 and others as 0
mad_bor_g1000_sum$mad_vs_global <- "Other"

fill <- function(x) {
  if (x["malagasy"] == 1) {
    x["mad_vs_global"] <- "Malagasy"
  } else {
    x["mad_vs_global"] <- x["population"]
  }
}

mad_bor_g1000_sum$mad_vs_global <- apply(mad_bor_g1000_sum, 1, FUN = fill)
```

```{r}
mad_bor_g1000_sum$Region <- "Other"

mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$population %in% c("Borneo", "Sumba", "Timor"), "Region"] <- "Island southeast Asia"
mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$population %in% c("Bengali", "Punjabi"), "Region"] <- "South Asia"
mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$population %in% c("Southern Han Chinese", "Kinh Vietnamese"), "Region"] <- "East Asia"
mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$population %in% c("Esan", "Gambian Mandinka", "Luhya", "Mende", "Yoruba"), "Region"] <- "Africa"
mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$malagasy == 1, "Region"] <- mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$malagasy == 1, "population"]
# wharerver is left as "Other" set to Africa
mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$Region == "Other", "Region"] <- "Africa"


ggplot(pcs, aes(
  x = V1, y = V2,
  colour = mad_bor_g1000_sum$Region,
  shape = as.factor(mad_bor_g1000_sum$malagasy)
)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = NULL,
    x = paste0("PC 1 (", round(variance$percent[1], 2), "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC 2 (", round(variance$percent[2], 2), "%)"),
    colour = NULL, shape = "none"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "right") +
  guides(
    shape = "none"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.line = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white")
  )

ggsave(paste0(res_dir, "pca_subsampled_regions_together.jpg"),
  width = 7, height = 7, dpi = 300
)
```

Altering the sample sizes reduces the explained variance of both principal components and increases the dispersion of the data.

## Recording R environment

Part of ensuring our workflow is reproducible is to keep track of the R environment.
We will automatically save our R environment into a file called `r_environment.json`.

```{r save-r-environment, echo=FALSE, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
filename_rmd <- "s04_full_pca.Rmd"
filename_renv <- paste0(
  res_dir, "/renv_",
  tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(filename_rmd)),
  ".json"
)
renv::lockfile_write(renv::lockfile_create(), file = filename_renv)

```
